restrictions: Ordinary collision of SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps from the standard IV: two 128-byte messages with the same random first block M0 and second blocks M1, M1' = M1 + DL (differences in words 8..12), followed by the common padding block. The second block is the transplanted advice pair with the state words A[6], A[7] released over a list of 169,908 (a2, W10) keys. The W17 condition is solved per F9 claw by a generic bit-sliced pass over the 7,960 distinct 18-bit prefixes of the keys; a prefix that passes is completed, tested on scalar words and, at a key hit, expanded to its mates.

Credited derivative of 3aa063d1 (Jbenisek, dariolina); replaces our refuted 165eb217. Time 98.5798 is total charged work plus headroom: the work cap (K = 8,309 operations per distinct claw, at least 1 percent above its formula; the pass a constant 19,566 with no folded code), the one-time setup (1,185,067,606 operations) and the 2^43 preprocessing. 343.1 trials per distinct claw (our own measured 99% lower bound); tail 2^-74.45 (declared bound). Memory 2^20.4095 = row sum 1,359,951 bytes plus 32,768, every row itemised, k4 code included (proof Section 6). Advice 1,344 bytes. Success 0.39.

heuristics.statement: For the selected-window distribution of the shipped program (KCAP=710, KTRY=32), the expected charged base-walk work per window is at most 463,618,904 operations, the yield is 58,959.42 distinct claw groups per window, and the distinct evaluated F9 claws per distinct claw are at most 0.016203. Chaining values of random first blocks behave as independent uniform values for the walk map and the later events; W17 is uniform over claws and listed keys; the 18 check bits of the pass are uniform, so that survivors per evaluated claw are at most 0.03111 in expectation.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r39-prefix-v1 and the program experiments/r39joint_k4.py with the shipped advice pair and list.
heuristics.extrapolation: The walk numbers are 99% one-sided bounds taken from 3aa063d1 (24 and 48 full windows). This entry ran 8 full windows on the same seeds; per-window base operations and F9-claw counts equal the published values exactly (proof Appendix A). Survivors: 579 in 20,480 sampled claws against 621.9 under the uniform model; the bound used is the one-sided 99% bound of that count. Extended to 2^81.167198 windows by independence of first blocks.
heuristics.limitations: The walk bounds are 3aa063d1's samples of 24 and 48 full windows on public seeds, reproduced exactly on the 8 windows this entry re-ran; the survivor sample (20,480 claws) was run by this entry. Each premise is at its own 99% bound, not jointly.

heuristics.statement: The W17 pass costs exactly 19,566 operations per evaluated F9 claw, for every claw: 733 + sum over the 21 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks), a formula of the shipped table evaluated by the program. It contains no folded or claw-specialised code; register spill, loop control, table loads and the constant words are inside the count. A survivor's counted cost is 711 + 563 per class tested, at most 2,963; a key hit costs at most 33,943,992; the one-time setup is charged 1,185,067,606 operations inside the claimed time. K = 8,309 is at least 1 percent above its formula.
heuristics.scope: The counted pass, survivor path, key-hit path and setup of experiments/r39joint_k4.py.
heuristics.extrapolation: The organizer experiment executes the full pass on every F9 claw of each trial (14 claws) and asserts the counted operations to the unit (F9 x (19,566 + 480) per trial). Run by this entry: 20,480 sampled claws, each without a survivor counting exactly the constant; 8 full windows fitting the formula. The scalar candidate routine priced at 560 counts 422 operations at the walk's prices. Setup charges: 1,024 per raw byte inflated by either reader, the counted candidate search and plane build of 3aa063d1's decoder, 256 per accepted lane, 256 per prefix, and 2^30 for everything else the import executes, the decoder's candidate search at this proof's prices included. The list sha256 is not executed on the attack path.
heuristics.limitations: The scalar routines of the survivor and key-hit paths are priced by stated composite charges, not executed through the counter; the setup charges for inflate, prefix sets and sorting are stated allowances. Both are bounded and inside the claimed time.

heuristics.statement: For a valid listed variant passing F8 in a claw passing F9 with W17 equal to the advice value, the two 39-step compressions give equal outputs with probability at least 2^-74.45. This is the declared bound QDECL of the shipped replica, below its hard-asserted one-sided 99.9% bound 2^-74.4326; the 14-run mean 2^-74.3238 is not used.
heuristics.scope: Rows 18 to 38 of the advice trail after rows 0 to 17 hold; parity classes pooled as in 5f8e6192.
heuristics.extrapolation: Fourteen organizer runs of experiments/r39tail.py (6,398 verified collisions in 45,875,200 proposals). The replica draws the advice values of W10 and W11; transfer to k = 4 variants rests on the joint arm reported by 3aa063d1 (ratio 2^+0.023, s.d. 0.026; 14 runs on 60,000 real variant triples).
heuristics.limitations: Public seeds, no organizer holdout. The transfer to the variant points is measured by 3aa063d1's joint arm (14 runs, 60,000 real variant triples).

heuristics.statement: A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 are fixed to the advice values; (A[6], A[7]) range over the listed keys and their mates; for every valid entry both messages follow the advice state-difference trail through step 15. Constructing and selecting the advice pair costs at most 2^43 compressions: 93 pair constructions of 2^36 each (2^34 candidate dense parts on steps 10 to 15, 4 compressions charged per candidate) plus 93 tail screens of 14 runs of 2^24 each, 2^42.545 in all (proof Section 9). The amount is added to the claimed time. Enumerating the list offline costs about 2^24 operations.
heuristics.scope: The one-time offline construction of the 160-byte advice pair (the pair of 5f8e6192) and of the weight-3 list: 361,638 valid entries, 169,908 keys, 35 shipped classes, 7,960 prefixes. Not part of the online walk.
heuristics.extrapolation: Trials 0 and 1 of experiment r39-transplant-claw execute verify_advice_construction(): the exact bit-by-bit fibre search solve_row_exact on rows 16 and 17 of the advice pair (g16_fibre_size = 2, g17_fibre_size = 1, fibre_dfs_ops = 1,944 word operations), the downward step inversion from steps 10 to 15 with zero search (downward_inv_ok = 1), and a 256-candidate slice of the step-15 free bits (advice_slice_cands = 256, advice_slice_hits = 1, ops_per_cand = 411 word operations = 0.146 compressions, charged as 4). Extended from the 256 candidates to the 2^34 candidate space by the dimension count 384 - 350 of 38912d66 Section 4.2, which agrees with the source paper's own measurement of about 2^34.2 SHA-256 calls for the step (ePrint 2026/1120 Section 4.3), and from one pair to the 93 pairs of the selection by multiplication (9993eaa8 Section 11). List counts are reproduced by an independent enumeration (5,489 masks, 204 passing F11, 61 with solutions, 386,788 passing F10, 361,638 keeping the trail); the key set of the shipped recipe equals that of the 361,638-entry list (asserted at build); the program asserts the decoded count at every import and, in the experiment entry, the sha256 of the decoded list.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer run executes one fibre search and 256 candidates, not the 2^34 space and not the 93-pair campaign, which the authors of the pair ran. The charge is the full declared cost of that campaign, with 4 compressions per candidate where 0.146 was counted, and the declared exponent 43 is 2^0.455 above the sum. Trail validity of the listed entries is checked by this entry's own enumeration.

heuristics.statement: Windows are independent (fresh first blocks). The trials of a claw are its keys with a valid mate in F8; their number is a property of the claw and varies between claws (proof Appendix B), and the count uses only its mean, at least 343.1 per distinct claw, the one-sided 99% lower bound of this entry's direct measurement. Given the claws of a window, the W17 events of distinct keys are independent with probability 2^-32 each (tested at a scaled event). Only the first hit of each window is counted: the budget divides lambda by 1 - 0.00254, the share of hits beyond the first, and the first hit succeeds with probability at least p_tail because every mate of a hit key is tested. No independence between the tails of different hits, or between mates of one key, is used.
heuristics.scope: The amplification over 2^81.167198 windows of the shipped program.
heuristics.extrapolation: Trials per claw: 22346.042 distinct listed keys with a valid mate in F8 per evaluated F9 claw (s.e. 161.579; 2,000 real F9 claws) times 938.875 distinct F9 claws per window (s.e. 8.909; 8 full windows) divided by 58,959.42 groups per window is 355.840 (s.e. 4.245); its one-sided 99% lower bound, estimate - 2.998 x s.e., is 343.113, priced as 343.1. Bracket (proof Section 7), in trials per distinct claw: organizer-observed floor 193.1 (keys whose shipped entry passes F8, 12,124 per claw on the organizer's 14 claws; their sum is asserted not smaller than 142,165), priced 343.1, measured 355.840, independent-mates model 375.8 (the list's key multiplicities at the rate 9/128). The priced figure is 3.6% under the measurement and 8.7% under the model. The base entries price 358.406 to 360.880 from larger enumerations. Organizer-run over all 169,908 keys of its 14 F9 claws: that F8 rate (7.14% against 9/128 = 7.03%) and the dispersion of scaled key hits (H-implicit-distinct-key-dispersion). First hits: a window holds 0.00506 hits on average at the upper bound of the trial count, so hits beyond the first are 0.254% of the hits, and lambda is divided by 1 - 0.00254.
heuristics.limitations: The trial count is this entry's measurement on 2,000 claws of 8 full windows; the organizer run supports its floor, 193.1, and the priced 343.1 lies under the measurement and under the independent-mates model. The groups-per-window figure 58,959.42 is 3aa063d1's and cancels in lambda. The 2^-32 W17 event is tested at its 2^-7 scaling. Independence between the tails of different hits is not a premise: only first hits are counted.

heuristics.statement: Mean work per window is at most 485,592,607 operations against the cap 489,893,820 (margin 0.87%), and the per-window s.d. is at most 15,508,843, when each of the four sample moments (mean and s.d. of the base walk, mean and s.d. of the distinct F9 claws per window) is replaced by its one-sided 99.75% upper confidence bound, so that the four hold together at 99%. For independent windows Chebyshev's inequality bounds the probability that the cap binds before B windows below 4.9e-24.
heuristics.scope: The work cap of k4_budget over B = 2^81.167198 windows.
heuristics.extrapolation: Samples: base walk, 24 full windows of this walk (3aa063d1 Appendix C: mean 461,649,658, s.d. 3,858,918); distinct F9 claws, 48 full windows (3aa063d1 H1-ops: mean 944.60, s.d. 35.37). The 8 full windows re-run by this entry are 8 of the 24 seeds; they reproduce the published per-window values exactly (proof Appendix A) and give 938.875 (s.d. 25.20) distinct F9 claws. Bounds: mean + t x s.d. / sqrt(n) with t(23) = 3.104, t(47) = 2.946; s.d. x sqrt((n - 1) / q), q the 0.25% chi-square quantile, 8.450 and 24.316. The pass is a constant of the program, so the other random parts are the survivors and the rare key hit, taken at their own bounds. The organizer's four pass-off windows reproduce 3aa063d1's operation counts on the same seeds to the unit (hard-asserted), so the cited samples are samples of the walk the organizer ran. The cap exceeds the sample mean of the work by 7.87 combined standard errors, and the Chebyshev figure leaves room for a far larger s.d. From these samples to 2^81.167198 independent windows by Chebyshev, with no distributional assumption on the total.
heuristics.limitations: The confidence bounds are normal-theory intervals on 24 and 48 public-seed windows. The margin left after the bounds is 0.87% of the cap (1.44% at the sample moments). Window independence is premise H1.

heuristics.statement: Given the claws, the W17 events of distinct keys are dispersed as independent trials. Tested in the organizer run at a scaled-down event of probability 2^-7 (the W17 value times 2654435761 mod 2^32 has its top 7 bits zero: the attack's event with its single target scaled up) on every key whose shipped entry passes F8, in every F9 claw of the four organizer windows: 14 claws, 169,731 key events, 1,319 hits against 1326.0 expected (z = -0.19), Pearson sum 12.63 on 14 degrees of freedom. The acceptance region is fixed in the manifest and hard-asserted by the program on the sums it measures: pooled hits within 2.576 standard deviations of expectation, and Pearson sum smaller than 29.14, the 99% quantile.
heuristics.scope: All 682 blocks of the per-key pass (all 169,908 keys) on all 14 F9 claws of the four organizer windows of r39k4-window-small.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the 2^-7 event to the single 2^-32 target on the same keys and the same W17 words: the scaled event is a hash of the full 32-bit W17 value, so it is the attack's event with a larger target set. On 5 further local seed sets (78 claws, run by this entry with the same program) the pooled count is 7,217 against 7,298 expected (z = -0.95).
heuristics.limitations: A proxy at probability 2^-7, on 14 claws and public seeds. One of the 14 claws has 117 hits for 95.4 expected (z = +2.22), where 0.6 such claws are expected; the pooled result is z = -0.19.
